mcqs.learning_point: Understand conditions for work to be done
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly defines the condition under which work is done in physics?

options.A: Work is done whenever a force is applied, regardless of motion.
options.B: Work is done only when a force causes a displacement of the point of application in the direction of the force.
options.C: Work is done only if the force is vertical.
options.D: Work is done only when the object's speed increases.

mcqs.answer: Work is done only when a force causes a displacement of the point of application in the direction of the force.
mcqs.explanation: In physics, work is defined as the product of the component of a force in the direction of displacement and the magnitude of that displacement (W = F·s). If there is no displacement or the displacement is perpendicular to the force, no work is done. Option B captures this definition, while the other options describe incorrect or incomplete ideas.

mcqs.learning_point: Calculate work using W = Fs for simple cases
mcqs.question: A constant horizontal force of 10 N pushes a box across a smooth floor for a distance of 5 m. What is the work done by the force?
mcqs.explanation: Work = Force × Displacement when the force and displacement are in the same direction. Here, W = 10 N × 5 m = 50 J. The other options result from incorrect multiplication or omission of units.

mcqs.learning_point: Use joule as the SI unit
mcqs.question: Which of the following quantities is expressed in joules (J)?

options.C: Work done when a 2 N force moves an object 3 m

mcqs.answer: Work done when a 2 N force moves an object 3 m
mcqs.explanation: Work = Force × Displacement, so 2 N × 3 m = 6 J, which is expressed in joules. Power is measured in watts, force in newtons, and battery energy is usually given in coulomb‑volts or watt‑hours, not directly in joules.

mcqs.question: A person lifts an 8‑kg book vertically upward through a height of 0.5 m at constant speed. Which statement best defines the work done on the book?

options.A: Work is the product of the book’s mass and the height lifted.
options.B: Work is the force applied multiplied by the displacement in the direction of the force.
options.C: Work is the energy lost due to friction during lifting.
options.D: Work is the time taken to lift the book multiplied by the applied force.

mcqs.answer: Work is the force applied multiplied by the displacement in the direction of the force.
mcqs.explanation: When lifting at constant speed, the applied force equals the weight (mg). Work = F × s = mg × h. Option B states the general definition of work. Options A, C, and D misuse the concepts of mass, friction, and time.

mcqs.question: A student claims that when a force acts on an object and the object moves, work is always done, even if the displacement is perpendicular to the force. Which part of this claim is incorrect?

options.A: A force must be present for work to be done.
options.B: Work is only done when the displacement has a component along the direction of the force.
options.D: Work depends on the mass of the object.

mcqs.answer: Work is only done when the displacement has a component along the direction of the force.
mcqs.explanation: Work equals the dot product of force and displacement (W = F·s = Fs cosθ). If the displacement is perpendicular (θ = 90°), cosθ = 0 and no work is done. The presence of force and the unit joule are correct statements, and work does not depend directly on mass.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand conditions for work to be done
mcqs.question: A block is pulled by a rope with a force of 30 N acting at 60° above the horizontal, moving the block 4 m horizontally. Does the rope do work on the block?

options.A: No, because the force is not entirely horizontal.
options.B: Yes, because there is a component of the force in the direction of displacement.
options.C: No, because the vertical component does no work.
options.D: Yes, because any force applied over a distance does work regardless of direction.

mcqs.answer: Yes, because there is a component of the force in the direction of displacement.
mcqs.explanation: Only the horizontal component (30 cos60° = 15 N) contributes to work. Work = (horizontal component) × displacement = 15 N × 4 m = 60 J. Option B correctly identifies the need for a component along the displacement; options A and C ignore the component concept, and D is too broad.

mcqs.learning_point: Calculate work using W = Fs for simple cases
mcqs.question:
Two scenarios are given:
Scenario I: A 20 N force pushes an object horizontally for 3 m.
Scenario II: A 10 N force pushes the same object horizontally for 6 m, but the force is applied at 60° to the horizontal.
Which scenario results in greater work done on the object?

options.A: Scenario I results in greater work.
options.B: Scenario II results in greater work.
options.C: Both scenarios produce the same amount of work.
options.D: The work cannot be compared without knowing the object's mass.

mcqs.answer: Scenario I results in greater work.
mcqs.explanation: Work = F cosθ × d. Scenario I: θ = 0°, work = 20 N × 3 m = 60 J. Scenario II: horizontal component = 10 cos60° = 5 N, work = 5 N × 6 m = 30 J. Therefore, Scenario I does more work. Mass is irrelevant for work calculation, so option D is incorrect.

mcqs.learning_point: Use joule as the SI unit
mcqs.question: A particle moves under a constant force of 5 N along a straight line. If the particle’s kinetic energy increases by 125 J, what is the displacement of the particle in the direction of the force?
mcqs.explanation: Work done on the particle equals the change in kinetic energy (Work–Energy Theorem). Thus, 125 J = 5 N × displacement ⇒ displacement = 125 J / 5 N = 25 m. Only option D satisfies this calculation; the other distances give incorrect work values.
